data.narrative:
Halter, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Craig Piggott, has raised $420M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of nine private peers and one public comparable (277810.KQ), all operating in the robotics and manufacturing sector. Key private comparables include Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $420M raised proxy, yielding $714M. Peer-median analysis benchmarks Halter against seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.6B and a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. These peers include both Series B and Series D-stage companies, reflecting some methodological spread.

Synthesizing both approaches produces a triangulated range of $607M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $1.2B. The stage-progression method anchors the lower bound, while the peer set's upper quartile (Exotec and Generalist AI at $2.0B) anchors the high case. Key uncertainties include Halter's specific revenue or deployment metrics relative to peers, stage progression assumptions in an inflationary funding environment, and the heterogeneity of Series B versus Series D comparables. The $1.2B median reflects typical Series C positioning within this peer cohort.
